title: Quantized serving: unsupported-op spike causing crashloops and accuracy drift — recovery playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Incident summary: Between 2025-03-09 22:15 UTC and 2025-03-10 00:40 UTC a deploy of the quantized-model converter introduced a fused op variant (fused_group_norm_v2) not recognized by the runtime's quant kernel selector. This caused a spike in operator fallback and increased memory churn on quantized serving nodes. A subset of pods entered crashloops due to a latent alignment bug in our quant-weight loader that manifests only when the runtime uses the fallback slow path. Several production customer workloads experienced accuracy drift (higher NLL, degraded BLEU on our eval prompts) and intermittent 5xx errors. Detection was via anomaly alerts from the console latency and error-rate dashboards and multiple customer support tickets.
timeline: 2025-03-09 21:30 UTC: Converter PR merged that added fused_group_norm_v2 fingerprinting (PR: github.com/redwood/convert/pull/882)
2025-03-09 22:10 UTC: Nightly canary deploy ran; limited traffic routed to canary pool (no errors observed in canary metrics)
2025-03-09 22:15 UTC: Staged converter artifact promoted to runtime conversion jobs for the hosted fleet
2025-03-09 22:45 UTC: First customer SLO alerts — increased p95 latency on several routes
2025-03-09 23:05 UTC: Crashloop alerts from quantized-serving pool in us-west-2; SRE paged
2025-03-09 23:20 UTC: Temporary routing rule put in place to divert traffic to non-quantized variants and a warm fallback cluster
2025-03-09 23:40 UTC: Revert of converter PR started (github.com/redwood/convert/pull/886) and hotfix build prepared
2025-03-10 00:05 UTC: Hotfix rollout completed; crashloops subsided, error rates trending down
2025-03-10 00:40 UTC: Accuracy regressions confirmed on canary eval suite; regression alert created and triage initiated
root_cause: The new fused_group_norm_v2 operator fingerprint introduced by the converter produced an op signature that the runtime incorrectly mapped to a fallback slow-path operator. The fallback code exercises a different quant-weight loading path which exposed an alignment assumption violation in the packed-weight reader, causing intermittent memory corruption under specific batching and KV-cache patterns. Because the converter change passed the limited canary (which did not include the long-sequence batching workload or the full eval prompt set), the issue slipped to production.
immediate_mitigation: Reverted converter change to stop emitting fused_group_norm_v2 fingerprints (PR: github.com/redwood/convert/pull/886) — reverted to previous stable converter
Temporary routing policy: route quantized traffic from affected customers to verified non-fallback variants and to dedicated warm nodes (policy change ID: policy-2025-03-09-01)
Applied runtime guard that rejects unknown fused op fingerprints with a clear error and instructs conversion to fallback to canonical ops (runtime patch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1515)
Expanded incident runbook steps so on-call can immediately revert converter artifacts and execute warm-routing within 10 minutes
long_term_actions: Operator canonicalization: add a canonicalization pass in the converter to map fused op variants to a small, well-tested set of runtime-supported ops (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-04-03)
Packed-weight loader hardening: audit and fix alignment assumptions, add sanitizer builds and deterministic fuzz tests for packed-weight parsing (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2025-03-31)

Canary expansion: include long-sequence, high-batch, and KV-cache-heavy workloads in canary evaluation; run the full eval prompt set used by the quality team during every converter change (owner: Lars Olsson, ETA: 2025-03-24)
Op compatibility matrix: publish an opsig compatibility matrix and enforce CI gate when converter emits ops not in the matrix (owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2025-03-28)
Runtime shim layer: implement an op shim to translate new fused variants to tested kernels until upstream kernels are available (owner: Marco Giordano, ETA: 2025-04-10)

Post-deploy regression detection: wire per-deploy automated evals that check a lightweight quality delta (NLL/BLEU/embedding-sim) and block promotion if regression > threshold (owner: Quality Team, ETA: 2025-04-01)

Observability: add operator-level ripple metrics (fallback rate, slow-path memory allocs) and correlate with model-version and converter-sha in the console (owner: Observability Team, ETA: 2025-03-27)

comments: 2025-03-10 01:15 UTC — Diego Morales: Observed that the crashloops occur only when request seq_len > 1024 and batch_size >= 8. Likely alignment path that only triggers with large KV cache allocations.
2025-03-10 02:05 UTC — Priya Nair: Reproduced memory mis-read locally by forcing fallback path and instrumenting packed-weight reader. Patch in progress: fix pointer arithmetic and add bounds checks.
2025-03-11 09:20 UTC — Sofia Patel (PM): Need customer comms drafts for affected accounts; recommend postmortem share with CSMs and AE team once long-term action timeline is firmer.
2025-03-12 16:40 UTC — Marco Giordano: Runtime guard has been merged to the staging branch. Performance impact negligible on normal paths; safe to roll behind feature flag.

2025-03-13 11:03 UTC — Lars Olsson: Added canary workload recipes to github.com/redwood/canary/quant-workloads and updated CI to run them on converter PRs. Waiting on infra quota increase for full parallel runs.
resolution_summary: Short-term: reverted offending converter change and rolled a runtime guard; traffic was routed away from vulnerable quantized pools and crashloops stopped within ~50 minutes of first alerts. Accuracy regressions were mitigated by routing customers to non-fallback variants. Long-term: schedule includes canonicalization in the converter, loader hardening, canary workload expansion, and CI gating to prevent future slip-throughs. Owners and timelines are assigned; critical code fixes are In Progress.
